summary: Native Node addon harvests Chromium cookies and login data with embedded HTTPS exfil client
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB Rust-compiled Node.js native addon (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) set as the package `main`, with no JS wrapper, no source, and a one-line README. Read-only strings in the binary include Chromium `Cookies` SQLite schema fragments (`FROM cookies`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX cookies_unique_index ON cookies(host_key, top_frame_site_key,...)`) and Chromium password-store output (`Found login for`), indicating code paths that open and parse the Chromium/Chrome Login Data and Cookies SQLite databases. The same binary links a full outbound TLS + HTTP stack (rustls handshake states, ureq crate) with HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY handling, together with host-fingerprinting routines (getifaddrs, gethostname, /etc/lsb-release, cpuinfo parsing). Because `main` points directly at the.node file, `require()`/`import` of the package auto-runs the addon's napi_register_module_v1 init code. The package name `new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu` and version string `3.1.42-origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-415-1785842368` are keyword-stuffed with a trailing Unix timestamp, mimicking the platform-specific optional-dep siblings of legitimate native toolchains.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
